steps.question: Which of the 12,000 genes differ in log2(TPM+1) expression between the 6 treated and 6 control muscle samples?

steps.description: Fit a per-gene linear model on the delivered log2(TPM+1) matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples) with condition (treated vs control) as the only covariate, using limma's empirical-Bayes moderation with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE — the documented route for continuous log-scale expression when no counts exist. Produce a full results table for every tested gene: gene ID, mean expression (AveExpr), log2 fold change (treated minus control, on the delivered log2 scale), moderated t, raw p, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and B statistic; plus a volcano plot, an MA-style plot of logFC vs AveExpr, and a heatmap of the top ~50 genes by FDR with samples annotated by condition. caveats: GO biological-process sets overlap heavily; blocks of correlated significant terms are expected and must not be reported as independent discoveries

steps.context: Input is the full per-gene table written by T1S1 (all tested genes, with gene ID and moderated t). Organism is Homo sapiens (taxon 9606), tissue muscle. Human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO biological-process (~7,500 sets) collections are staged as symbol-based GMT files in the environment's pathway references; the human WikiPathways collection is also present as an optional third view.
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are coordinately shifted between treated and control muscle, given the full moderated-t ranking from the limma-trend contrast?
constraints: Rank genes by the signed moderated t statistic from T1S1, not by logFC alone and not by p-value magnitude alone
Use the T1S1 tested-gene list as the ORA universe — never the full annotation background
Use human gene sets only; do not substitute mouse or rat collections
Report GSEA as the primary readout and ORA as secondary, given n=6 per group limits per-gene significance

If the human hallmark or GO gene-set resources are not present at run time, report which collection was missing and proceed with whichever staged human collection is available, stating the substitution; do not fail the step over an absent optional collection
steps.description: Take the complete per-gene results table from T1S1 and run rank-based gene set enrichment (fgsea) on the full gene ranking, ranked by the moderated t statistic (signed, so direction is preserved), against human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets — both resolved from the environment's staged pathway references for Homo sapiens. Report normalized enrichment scores, p-values, BH-adjusted p-values, set size, and leading-edge genes for the top sets in both directions. Secondarily, if T1S1 yielded at least ~50 genes at FDR<0.05, also run over-representation analysis of that significant subset (split by direction) against the same collections using the tested-gene universe from T1S1 — not all annotated genes. Because GO-BP sets are hierarchically nested, collapse redundant parent/child hits before reporting a count of significant processes.
acceptance_criteria: The fraction of T1S1 tested genes whose identifiers match the gene symbols in the staged human gene-set files is reported explicitly; if overlap is below ~50%, the step must state that the identifier spaces disagree and that the enrichment result is unreliable, rather than reporting enrichment as if valid
fgsea run on the full signed moderated-t ranking against human hallmark sets, with NES, p, BH-adjusted p, size and leading edge reported
fgsea also run against human GO biological-process sets, with nested/redundant sets collapsed before any count of significant processes is stated
Enrichment results written as a table and visualized (e.g. NES bar plot or dot plot for the top sets in each direction)

Over-representation analysis is run only if the T1S1 FDR<0.05 list has at least ~50 genes, and when run uses the T1S1 tested-gene set as the universe; if skipped, the reason and the actual DE gene count are stated
Species used for all gene sets is Homo sapiens, matching the data

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE from log2 TPM (limma-trend)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample matrix of log2(TPM+1) values (/data/inputs/expression/log_expr.csv) with a 12-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) giving one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. No counts were delivered, so the count-based negative-binomial route (DESeq2/edgeR) is not applicable — running it on log2 TPM would silently violate its distributional assumption. The correct method for continuous, already-log-transformed expression is a linear model per gene with empirical-Bayes moderation of the residual variance: limma with trend=TRUE (mean-variance trend fitted on the log scale) and robust=TRUE, which is limma's documented handling of log-CPM/log-TPM-like input when counts are unavailable. Step T1S1 does exactly that, after the two pieces of due diligence log-scale TPM demands: verifying the matrix really is on a log scale (max value, no negatives) and rather than assuming, and filtering out genes with near-zero expression/variance across all 12 samples, which otherwise inflate the trend fit and waste multiple-testing budget. T1S2 provides the unsupervised sanity check — PCA and sample correlation heatmap — that tells us whether condition is the dominant axis of variation or whether an outlier sample drives the DE list; it runs in parallel with T1S1 because it does not depend on the contrast. T2S1 takes the ranked result from T1S1 into gene-set space. With n=6 per group, per-gene power is limited, so the ranked-list method (GSEA on the full moderated-t ranking via fgsea) is the primary readout and over-representation of the FDR-significant subset is secondary and reported only if that subset is large enough to be meaningful. Human hallmark and GO-BP sets are staged under /mnt/refs and match the organism (Homo sapiens, taxon 9606). Note the tissue is muscle, so gene symbols are expected to be HGNC-compatible with the staged GMTs; the step must report the fraction of the 12,000 features that map, since a low overlap would indicate a non-symbol identifier space and invalidate the enrichment rather than just weaken it.
